passes.reasoning: Claim 2: L2a and L6a compare the learner with fixed rules at equal budget. The fixed rules' calibration labels are charged and counted as hits, and the free-label static arm is only an upper bound, so the baseline has no information advantage. The learner's ratios are 1.05 to 1.14 in L2a and 1.06 to 1.13 in L6a, and the CIs exclude 1. L7b also passes. Claim 3: E04 is a different proxy (answer-only judge) from E01. Its embedding AUC gain is about -0.0003 to -0.003, below 0.05, and its neighbor ratio is 1.00, below 1.5. L1a agrees. The free-label confound is controlled, so W2 is false. The ledger holds claim 3 as killed or not supported, so W3 is false.

Claim 3: E04 (different proxy, judge models) reports embedding delta AUC about -0.0003 and neighbor ratio 1.00, so both are under the thresholds. L1a agrees (PC delta +0.009). Claim 2: L1b, L2a, L6a and L7b compare against fixed rules whose calibration labels are charged. They have equal budgets and no free labels. The learner is 1.04 to 1.14 times the best fixed rule, with CIs excluding 1 (L6a: 1.068, 1.060, 1.129, 1.072). Scope is limited: the edge reverses at 10% budget and ties on E01. W2 is false because the confound was controlled. W3 is false because the standing view on claim 3 is that it is not supported.

Claim 2: L1b/L2a/L6a compare the learner against fixed rules whose calibration labels are charged to the same budget, with no free labels. L2a gives ratios 1.05 to 1.14 with intervals above 1. L6a gives 1.06 to 1.13 against the strongest amortized fixed rule. So the free-label confound is controlled. The edge reverses at 10% budget and on E01, so support is conditional. Claim 3: E04 is a different proxy (answer-only judge) from E01. It shows an embedding AUC gain of about 0 (-0.0003) and a neighbor ratio of 1.00. L1a confirms this. Both thresholds for killed are met. The ledger does not assert claim 3 is supported, so W3 is false.
